key_insight: PA-SciML shifts agentic SciML from choosing the lowest-error surrogate to verifying each candidate against explicit physics checks before calling it acceptable.
engineering_relevance: For computational mechanics, this means surrogate models can be screened for boundary-condition compliance, scaling behavior, and causality, reducing the risk of deploying accurate-but-unphysical predictors.
method: Fix the scoring evaluator before the search begins and derive machine-checkable physics requirements.
Train and audit each candidate surrogate on predicted outputs, then search for high-violation cases over input/load-history ranges without using reference fields.
Optionally run numerical probes before training and test one modeling change at a time to log isolated improvements.
evidence_signal: In the reported solid-mechanics examples, the static case found a lower-error surrogate that still passed linear-elastic checks, while in the transient case an error-only baseline with similar mean error failed a causality check but the selected surrogate passed.
watch_item: Physics verification is only as strong as the chosen audit rules, so missing or overly narrow checks could still let unphysical models slip through.
paper_title: Physics-Audited Agentic Discovery in Scientific Machine Learning
